question: Yash travels 252 km at 63 km/hr, the next 891 km at 99 km/hr and the next 183 km at 61 km/hr. What is his average speed (in km/hr) for the whole journey? (Round off your answer to two decimal places)
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Distance = 252 + 891 + 183 = 1326 km

Total Time = (252 ÷ 63) + (891 ÷ 99) + (183 ÷ 61) = 4 + 9 + 3 = 16 hours

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time = 1326 ÷ 16 = 82.875 km/hr

Rounding off 82.875 to two decimal places gives 82.88 km/hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 82.88 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed for Equal Distances

If a person travels two equal distances at speeds S₁ and S₂, then Average Speed = (2 × S₁ × S₂) ÷ (S₁ + S₂).

Relative Speed

For objects moving in the same direction, Relative Speed = S₁ − S₂. For objects moving in opposite directions, Relative Speed = S₁ + S₂.

Unit Conversion

To convert speed from km/hr to m/s, multiply the value by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/hr, multiply by 18/5.
